sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for project page
sections.what: Brings in the metadata type, the not-found helper, the navigation, the project detail view and the project lookup.
sections.why: Keeps each piece reusable and the data in one place.

sections.name: generateStaticParams
sections.title: Lists every project address
sections.what: Tells the build the full list of project slugs so each project gets its own prepared page.
sections.why: Needed because the site is built as static files; without it the project pages would not exist.
sections.watch_out: Two projects with the same slug would collide.

sections.name: generateMetadata
sections.title: Per-project title and description
sections.what: Gives each project page its own browser title and description; unknown projects get no metadata.
sections.why: Likely reason: so shared links show the right project name.
sections.watch_out: An unknown slug gets no title, while its page shows not-found.

sections.name: ProjectPage
sections.title: Project page or not-found
sections.what: Finds the project for the address. If none exists, shows a not-found page; otherwise shows the navigation and the full project detail.
sections.why: Guards against bad addresses so visitors never see a broken page.
sections.watch_out: This page reads params directly, which may need changing with newer framework versions.

summary: The page for one project, prepared ahead of time for each project in the data; unknown project addresses show a not-found page.
purpose: Shows the full details of each build at its own address.
why: Reason for the advance preparation is not stated in the code. Likely reason: the site is built as static files, so each project address is generated in advance.
how: 1) Lists every project slug so the build creates one page per project. 2) Sets the title and description from the project. 3) Looks up the project from the address; if none exists, shows a not-found page. 4) Renders the navigation and the project detail component.
inputs: The slug from the web address, and the project list.
outputs: A project page, or a not-found result for an unknown slug.
risks: The params value is read directly. In some newer Next.js versions params can arrive asynchronously, so check the framework version before upgrading. A project removed from the data leaves no page.
debug: If a project page is missing after a build, check that the project has a slug in the project data. If titles are blank, check the punchline field.
